RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Rowan Lawson
Member ID: W383949058
Reference Number: POC-F37F115FED-48372
Date of Notice: 2026-08-23
Requested Service: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
Treating Surgeon: [Dr.] Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Grievances and Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar decompression/discectomy), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-23. The stated reason for denial is that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window identified in the notice (deadline 2027-02-19).

Basis for review

Anthem has indicated that spine surgery requests such as this are reviewed against the Carelon Medical Benefits Management "Spine Surgery" Clinical Appropriateness Guideline (the version in effect on the date of this determination, effective 11/15/2025, Doc ID MSK03-1125.1-UC0126), specifically the "Lumbar Discectomy, Foraminotomy, and Laminotomy" subsection, which lists CPT 63030 among its covered codes. That subsection states that it "addresses lumbar discectomy, foraminotomy, and laminotomy when performed as elective, non-emergent procedures and not as part of the care of an acute or traumatic event." My requested surgery falls squarely within this scope, as an elective, non-emergent procedure for a chronic degenerative condition.

I was not able to obtain the complete text of the "Clinical Indications" portion of that subsection. The only additional language I have been able to confirm directly from the guideline is a partial excerpt indicating that the guideline recognizes as a qualifying indication: "Initial disc herniation when ALL of the following criteria are met: Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:" — the remainder of that bulleted list was not accessible to me. Because I have not been able to review the full criteria in this section, I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that Anthem/Carelon provide me and Dr. Reyes with a complete copy of "the specific rule, guideline, protocol, or other similar criterion" relied upon in denying this request, as required under applicable ACA and ERISA claims-procedure regulations. Beyond the fragment quoted above, the arguments below are stated in my own words and are not quotations of plan or guideline language.

Why the clinical record supports medical necessity

Based on the partial criteria language available to me, and based on generally accepted standards for lumbar discectomy/decompression, the relevant considerations appear to include: (1) radicular pain with functional impairment and physical exam findings correlating to radiculopathy or nerve root compression; and (2) imaging correlating to the clinical presentation. My clinical record satisfies these elements:

- Duration and severity of symptoms: I have experienced 24 months of progressive lower back pain that is not relieved by rest, indicating a chronic, worsening condition rather than a self-limited episode.

- Imaging correlation: MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-06-30 demonstrates an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is an objective, imaging-confirmed structural lesion at a specific level.

- Radicular symptoms and functional impairment: I have radicular pain radiating into my right calf and cannot stand for more than 10 minutes at a time. This represents a significant functional impairment consistent with L5 nerve root involvement.

- Correlating physical exam findings: My exam is documented as positive on provocative testing on the affected (right) side, with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on imaging (L4-L5/L5 nerve root) — i.e., the physical exam findings correlate with the radiculopathy and nerve root compression shown on MRI, which is the same correlation the guideline fragment I was able to obtain describes as a qualifying indication.

- Failed conservative treatment: I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-04-20 through 2026-06-29) including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note, without resolution of symptoms. I also completed 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-13 that produced only 2 weeks of partial relief. This represents a substantial, well-documented course of conservative management that has failed to resolve my symptoms.

- No contraindications: There is no active infection, no untreated substance use disorder, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker — none of which present any known barrier to surgery.

Taken together, this record demonstrates a chronic, imaging-confirmed nerve root compression with correlating radicular symptoms and physical exam findings, ongoing significant functional impairment, and a documented, multi-modal failure of conservative treatment (physical therapy, medication, and injection) over several months. I respectfully submit that this clinical picture meets the medical-necessity standard that the plan's own guideline is intended to capture, based on the portion of that guideline I have been able to review, and ask that Anthem obtain and apply the full text of its criteria to this same record.

Requested action

I respectfully request that Anthem:
1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Reyes; or
2. In the alternative, provide the complete "Lumbar Discectomy, Foraminotomy, and Laminotomy" clinical indications criteria that were actually applied to this request, and specify which sub-criterion, if any, my record is believed not to satisfy, so that I and my surgeon can respond with any additional supporting documentation; and
3. Arrange a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Reyes and the reviewing physician, as referenced in the general clinical appropriateness framework of the applicable guideline.

Enclosed with this appeal, please find: the physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-20 to 2026-06-29), documentation of NSAID trial and the 2026-04-13 corticosteroid injection, the 2026-06-30 MRI report and images, and Dr. Reyes's clinical notes documenting exam findings and functional limitations.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide written notice of the outcome within the timeframe required by applicable law and the plan's Evidence of Coverage. If this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I intend to pursue an external review through the Georgia Department of Insurance.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Rowan Lawson
